packageRules.description: The release tag (ABYSS_VERSION, a Dockerfile ARG with a `# renovate: datasource=github-releases depName=zephel01/Abyss` comment) is the only thing Renovate tracks; a postUpgradeTask fills the two companion pins (ABYSS_COMMIT, ABYSS_ENGINE_SHA256) after the bump. The schedule is weekly on purpose: the org's CI billing is paid-plan minutes, so the new repo's cadence is capped at weekly (zephel01/Abyss ships ~4.7 releases a day - daily checks would multiply the CI build gate by 7). The task is best-effort: hosted Mend Renovate blocks arbitrary postUpgradeTask commands unless they are allowlisted (docs.renovatebot.com/mend-hosted/faq, "How can I run arbitrary commands"), so the CI build check (.github/workflows/abyss-image.yml) is the enforcement.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ The `ABYSS_COMMIT` and `ABYSS_ENGINE_SHA256` pins in `Dockerfile` are auto-filled by the postUpgradeTask (`.github/renovate/abyss-pins.mjs`): it reads the bumped `ABYSS_VERSION`, resolves the tag's commit and the release's `SHA256SUMS`, and rewrites the two ARGs in place. The task only runs where the command is allowlisted - hosted Mend blocks arbitrary commands - so if the pins are still stale in this PR, the CI build check (`.github/workflows/abyss-image.yml`) is the enforcement: the PR must not pass it while the pins are stale. If the build fails on a pip pin, re-measure the pinned list (the comment above the `pip install` in the Dockerfile) and update it in the same PR.

After merge, CI publishes `ghcr.io/trollaus/abyss-image:sha-<ABYSS_COMMIT short>` (plus `latest` on master) and prints the image digest at the end of the run. Update flow: copy that digest line into the role's image reference (`abyss.image`, documented in the consuming role's README) in the parent repo's host_vars, then deploy the role (e.g. `--tags abyss`).
